final.answer: The valve FV-104-2 operated by loop FIC-104-2 is a Fisher ET/easy-e type control valve whose documentation lists several trim options: standard trims (e.g. trims 1, 4, 27, 28, 29, 37/37H with PTFE or metal seating), the Whisper Trim III and Whisper NXG Trim cages, Cavitrol III cage trim (trim 76), WhisperFlo aerodynamic cages, TSO (Tight Shutoff) trim, and a Trim Cartridge option, with NACE sour-service trims (85/87) also available. For high pressure drop and especially aerodynamic noise in gaseous service, the Whisper-family trims are the noise-attenuation option — Whisper Trim III and Whisper NXG Trim cages (with port-size-specific capability tables); WhisperFlo cages are also aerodynamic noise-attenuation cages. For very high pressure drops with cavitation protection, the Cavitrol III cage (trim 76) is offered, and trims 4 and 29 can be used up to 99 bar / 1440 psi pressure drop with clean dry gas. The description does not state which specific trim was actually selected for this valve.

final.answer: GV-1-2 is a globe valve in the discharge line from pump P-1-1, upstream of ball valve PV-1-1. A globe valve passing fluid when it should be shut is usually caused by seat or disc damage — wear, erosion, or debris (e.g., a particle or weld slug) lodged on the sealing face — or a stem/disc connection failure that prevents the disc from seating. Fix it by closing upstream and downstream isolation (note PV-1-1 downstream) and depressurizing/draining the line, then inspect: lap or re-seat the disc and seat ring or replace the trim, replace the gasket if the leak is at the bonnet or flanges, and verify the disc is properly attached to the stem and the valve is fully turned to the closed position before returning to service.
